status: exploratory generation design, not implemented; both inline and named style blocks plus implicit frontend are accepted human requirements
syntax_example: style "Describe the appearance" or style Workspace "Describe the appearance", each followed by ordinary Then children; frontend is implicit
ownership: Canonical declaring owner + style-block identity, explicit for named blocks and managed internally for inline blocks; each block has compiler-owned root and component/part hooks.
output: Accepted scoped CSS + one small generated record containing canonical scope, relevant input digest, selected/effective agent identity and artifact path; candidate/attempt state is separate from accepted output.
generation_inputs: static component structure and style hooks for the scope
shared renderer/theme asset versions relevant to those templates
effective generator/model recipe captured for each explicit attempt, separate from ordinary-build source/target compatibility
ordinary_builds: Consume current tracked CSS without AI calls or generation credentials. Validate relevant source/template/theme/target compatibility; missing/stale source inputs diagnose. Direct CSS edits are permitted and marked modified since generation. Changing configured provider/model only affects future generation and reports recipe drift, never silently replaces or invalidates otherwise compatible current CSS.
regeneration: Explicit headless preparation creates a candidate; an authoring agent can inspect/check and accept it, optionally as a composed operation. No required human preview/approval; failure retains current output.
application_boundary: existing source owns composition, data, bindings, permissions, forms/errors/focus behavior; generation emits scoped presentation CSS for the declared subtree
open_decisions: prompt-only versus optional typed overrides (human chose keep exploring)
placement and precedence of optional agent overrides (source, generation command, or both); omitted agent uses frontend
precise grammar/CLI spelling, profile declaration and generated record location; support for both inline and named blocks is settled
persistent inline block identity across edits and named-block namespace/collision rules
structured candidate validation/acceptance protocol and precise relevant-input/profile invalidation
how to qualify responsive/accessibility states without treating static checks as proof

agent_selection.required_outcome: Use the shared frontend coding-agent profile by default when agent is omitted. Identify the effective agent in the saved result without requiring repetitive source attributes; do not implicitly inherit the active chat agent.
agent_selection.candidate: Optional owning source profile reference, resolved through proposed shared root generation-tool configuration; provider/model settings normally live in that tooling config.
agent_selection.alternative: Optional explicit generation-command profile/tool/model override, recorded for that attempt; see design/proposals/build-generation/proposal.json.
agent_selection.profile_contents: Provider, requested model/version, coding-agent recipe/tool versions and effective generation settings; secrets are environment bindings, never generated source.
agent_selection.saved_identity: Record selected profile and effective recipe, requested provider/model and actual provider-reported model/version when available. Mark unavailable resolved identity rather than claiming it was pinned.
agent_selection.status: Default frontend is required by the human. Source versus command placement and precedence of optional overrides remain open; no frontend provider or coding agent has been selected or invoked.
agent_selection.default: frontend; authors need no agent= attribute or --agent flag for ordinary styling generation

lifecycle.status: Inspect accepted result, current/stale/missing status, saved agent identity and any pending or failed attempt.
lifecycle.generate: Explicitly capture the current scope inputs and effective agent recipe, then create a new candidate. Use this for first output, changed prompts or a deliberate new design; it can run even when accepted output is current.
lifecycle.retry: Require an explicit selected style unit/failed attempt; create another candidate from its captured inputs/recipe. Keep its current CSS and every other unit unchanged; never retry all units by default.
lifecycle.reset: Discard/supersede pending work for the explicitly selected unit only, preserving current CSS/direct edits and all other units. No AI call or deletion of saved styles.
lifecycle.accept: Promote only the selected CSS/metadata group while relevant captured inputs, current selected bytes and attempt state match. Unselected units/global assets stay intact; conflicting or late results remain candidates.
lifecycle.rollback: Restore an earlier accepted CSS/record pair through retained source-control history; diagnose incompatibility with current relevant inputs rather than silently using stale output.
lifecycle.shared_defaults: Returning permanently to shared styling is a separate authoring change that removes/disables the prompt style scope; deleting its saved file alone produces missing output, not regeneration.
lifecycle.failure: Provider failure, timeout, rejected output or cancellation retains accepted CSS. An unknown provider outcome is shown as unknown; recover by provider attempt/request identity where supported, otherwise require an explicit fresh retry with possible duplicate cost visible.
lifecycle.refine: Capture current edited CSS, owning intent/templates/theme and refinement instruction; generate an isolated candidate from that baseline.

command_examples.rollback: restore a compatible previous accepted CSS/record pair using source control
command_examples.note: Illustrative unimplemented agent-facing commands. TaskList is an optional source name; inline blocks are selected by internal ID from structured inspect/status. No target does not mean all; no interactive picker or human review required.
command_examples.inline_targeting: Resolve the inline block ID through structured inspect/status and target it programmatically; editor integration is optional. Exact selector spelling remains open.
command_examples.refine: can gen refine Todos.TaskList "Make only this list more compact."

syntax_forms.shared_behavior: Both forms style their nested Then components, use frontend by default and share the same saved-output/generate/retry/reset/accept lifecycle.
syntax_forms.name: An optional author-chosen label for this style block, not a keyword or a reusable component definition. Named blocks can be explicitly targeted by tools; inline blocks require no author-written identifier.
syntax_forms.agent_override: agent=otherProfile remains an optional override if source overrides are adopted; it is never required for either form.

scope_identity.required_outcome: Associate each inline or named block with its own accepted CSS and generation attempts; names are optional authoring syntax, not a prerequisite for saved styling.
scope_identity.named: Use the optional name within its defining ownership/namespace; namespace and collision rules still need precise design.
scope_identity.inline: Tooling owns persistent internal identity exposed by structured inspect/status with owner/source mapping. Editor selection is optional, never required. Current source position alone is not a stable saved identity.
scope_identity.identity_vs_freshness: Keep block identity separate from the relevant-input digest. Editing a prompt makes the existing result stale rather than implicitly assigning another block its CSS.
scope_identity.ambiguous_edits: Do not silently attach an accepted artifact to a different block after moves, copies or ambiguous matching. Exact identity persistence and edit reconciliation remain unimplemented design work.
scope_identity.current_gap: Bounded compiler scan found source-span/process-local identities, not persisted identities stable across edits: syntax/cst.rs SyntaxNode; analysis/mod.rs NodeKey; codegen/ir.rs IrUi and view-use IDs; codegen/js.rs presentation occurrence IDs. Existing artifact source revision/maps do not bridge this gap.

custom_views: Style blocks also belong inside reusable view definitions. Generate the definition-scoped CSS once and apply it safely to each render occurrence; custom prompt-rendered views are covered by design/proposals/build-generation/proposal.json.
direct_refinement: Tracked editable CSS is a primary build input accessible to the .can authoring agent. Original generated identity is historical; edited bytes are not silently attributed to that generator. Full provider/config/refinement controls are in design/proposals/build-generation/proposal.json.
targeting: Each style block is independently selectable, named or inline. Retry/refine/fresh/reset/accept act only on its own candidate/output group. Preserve every other style unit and current selected CSS; precise nested-cascade/shared-view boundaries remain open.
